name: 278. ElevenLabs speech stream keeps its final chunk (elevenlabs speech stream final chunk)
description: Pins TXE-5677. The ElevenLabs speech-stream read loop checked the read error before forwarding the bytes of the same read, so when the upstream answered with Content-Length and returned its last bytes together with io.EOF, those bytes were dropped and speech.audio.done was still sent: a short answer arrived as done with no audio, a longer one lost up to 4 KB of its end (TXE-4880's reproduction on v2.1.1 and v2.3.2). The loop now forwards the bytes first and handles the error after. These cases go through /v1/audio/speech with stream_format sse on the built-in elevenlabs provider. Case A is a short input, the shape that lost all of its audio: against a Content-Length upstream it is red on the old loop (done with no audio) and green on the fix. Case B is a longer input whose stream spans several reads and pins the several-delta contract; the client cannot know how many bytes the upstream sent (the gateway strips Content-Length from the headers it forwards), so B does not detect a lost tail. Both require non-empty audio, exactly one speech.audio.done as the last speech event, and no error event. Whether the live upstream answers with Content-Length decides whether the old loop lost bytes there; the byte-exact red/green pins are the Go tests TestElevenlabsSpeechStream* in core/streamfallback_test.go.
